name: Load balancer
kid: A traffic warden. Lots of computers could answer, so it picks one that isn’t busy, and sends every parcel of your video to that same one.
nerd: An L4 load balancer holds the service address (VIP). It hashes each connection’s 5-tuple onto a healthy backend (consistent hashing, as in Maglev), so every packet of one TCP connection reaches the same server; health checks take broken servers out.

1995.kid: Drawn as today. In 1995 there was only one web computer, so nobody needed to pick one.
1995.nerd: Drawn as today. Load balancers came later in the 1990s, as busy sites outgrew one server; in 1995 this site’s one web server answered everyone.
